technical.lead: (Mula sa Ingles na buod ngayong araw) FMRB EO T-2: DOE CESER joins witness slate, ABA + NAAG amicus
technical.body: (Mula sa Ingles na buod ngayong araw) The Frontier Model Review Board executive-order interagency-review push enters the two-business-day window before the May 15 14:00 EDT S-407 classified threshold briefing. Senate Cyber Subcommittee staff release a Wednesday-morning hearing-readiness memo confirming the witness slate firms to seven with the addition of the Department of Energy Cyber Security, Energy Security, and Emergency Response Assistant Secretary, joining the previously-confirmed NIST Director Locascio, ODNI cyber lead, NSA Cybersecurity Directorate director, Microsoft Threat Intelligence Center representative, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Director, and Federal Communications Commission Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau Chief. The American Bar Association Cybersecurity Legal Task Force and the National Association of Attorneys General AI working group file a joint Wednesday amicus letter joining the now-fourteen-organization coalition, narrowing focus to the per-state attorney-general consultation pathway plus AISI cyber-evaluation reciprocity 120-day placement window alignment. The House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology issues a Wednesday-afternoon follow-up press release confirming a coordinated request bundle with the Senate Cyber Subcommittee for the parallel 30-day House technical review window. White House OSTP holds the line that the executive order draft remains in interagency review with no signing window before May 22.

technical.lead: (Mula sa Ingles na buod ngayong araw) Indo-Pacific reciprocity adds Brazil + South Africa, hits 12
technical.body: (Mula sa Ingles na buod ngayong araw) The Indo-Pacific cyber-evaluation reciprocity perimeter crosses a fresh twelve-jurisdiction count on Wednesday with the first formal Latin American mirror-signature commitment plus the first African exploratory observer. Brazil's Cybersecurity Authority (ANCiber) publishes a Wednesday entry note converting its prior open-ended observer interest into a formal exploratory-observer commitment with a 240-day national-consultation window targeting Q2 2027 mirror signature, citing the OECD GENAI working-group baseline plus the Chile and Mexico Tuesday cross-hemispheric extension as the procedural precedent. South Africa's Cybersecurity Hub plus the Department of Communications and Digital Technologies separately announce a parallel exploratory-observer track with a 270-day consultation window — the first African entry into the cohort. The cohort now spans twelve named candidates (Singapore, Japan, South Korea, New Zealand formally; Canada, Australia, India, Taiwan, Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, Brazil as observers; South Africa as exploratory observer) plus the originating UK and EU. The OECD GENAI working-group secretariat publishes a Wednesday procedural note describing the cohort as on track toward the first thirteen-jurisdiction formal mirror count by Q3 2026.

technical.lead: (Mula sa Ingles na buod ngayong araw) AutoGen CVE-2026-44918 extends agent-loader taxonomy to nine CVEs
technical.body: (Mula sa Ingles na buod ngayong araw) A ninth agentic-AI tooling-stack CVE drops on Wednesday morning Pacific time, extending the eight-CVE Trail of Bits Tuesday taxonomy to a fresh tier-spanning instance. AutoGen CVE-2026-44918 (CVSS 8.6) is a path-traversal vulnerability in the workflow-state checkpoint loader that lets an attacker overwrite arbitrary host paths during checkpoint restore, mirroring the LangGraph CVE-2026-44712 deserialization pattern but with a different exploitation surface; the AutoGen maintainer team ships v0.6.4 same-day with the patch plus a paired backport advisory for the v0.5.x and v0.4.x branches the NHS England blocklist references. Trail of Bits publishes a Wednesday extended addendum updating its Tuesday taxonomy from eight to nine agent-checkpoint-and-manifest-loader CVEs, reaffirming the signed-checkpoint plus manifest-allowlist-validation common-mitigation pattern now extended with workflow-state path-canonicalization as the third tier. DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft co-publish a Wednesday joint follow-up addendum v2 (arxiv 2605.06712v2) extending the Tuesday runtime-verifier paper to the workflow-state tier.

technical.lead: (Mula sa Ingles na buod ngayong araw) Cerebras consolidates near $196; SEC ships 2nd sample comment letter
technical.body: (Mula sa Ingles na buod ngayong araw) Cerebras CBRS Wednesday session prints a textbook second-trading-week consolidation. The opening print at $195.40 lifts the stock 0.7 percent from Tuesday's $194.10 close, with the intraday range tight at $193.80-$197.60 and the close at $195.80, trailing-five-session turnover crossing $5.6B with the institutional-buyside cumulative net position estimated at 33 percent of float. Morgan Stanley reiterates the best-ideas-list at the $192 target and adds an explicit upside-tilt scenario at $235; Wells Fargo Securities initiates Buy at $208; Bernstein holds the $172 Market-Perform floor but acknowledges the consolidation pattern materially reduces the single-counterparty concentration discount. The SEC Division of Corporation Finance posts a Wednesday-morning EDGAR release that pairs a second sample comment letter on AI-services-revenue measurement basis (specifically addressing usage-tiered hyperscaler contract recognition timing plus committed-purchase-order treatment ambiguity) with a topical comment template on hyperscaler-anchor warrant-equity counterparty disclosure shape; Corp Fin staff working notes flagged in the Tenstorrent submission-acknowledgement working file cite both releases as additions to the operative precedent set. SambaNova publishes a Wednesday confidential-submission cover-letter draft for late-June filing.

technical.lead: (Mula sa Ingles na buod ngayong araw) SGLang + TGI default signed loader; Unsloth lands workflow-state fix
technical.body: (Mula sa Ingles na buod ngayong araw) SGLang RadixArk v0.5.7 and Hugging Face TGI v3.2.0 Wednesday point releases ship the signed-checkpoint loader as the documented default for new installs, becoming the second and third open-source serving stacks to land the primitive at the serving tier — with SGLang the first to default it; TGI ships in parallel. Yotta Labs canonical benchmark refresh places the shared-prefix workload at approximately 17,140 tok/s on vLLM v0.11.3 (up 3 percent from Tuesday) versus 18,860 tok/s on SGLang RadixArk v0.5.7 (up 4 percent from Tuesday) — the throughput gap holds at 9.1 percent essentially flat from Tuesday's 9.4 percent. Cloudflare Infire L40S edge-tier advantage closes to 1.12x (vs 1.18x Tuesday) with parity projected at vLLM v0.11.4 on Monday May 18. Unsloth ships its Wednesday changelog adding a quad-Hopper kernel-fused tensor-parallel forward-and-backward pass plus a deterministic workflow-state path-canonicalization mitigation tied to the AutoGen CVE-2026-44918 Wednesday disclosure, becoming the first local-LLM fine-tuning stack to ship the workflow-state mitigation alongside the signed-checkpoint primitive ahead of the framework cohort's coordinated mid-June default-shipment target.
